narrative: The model estimates a 13.0% probability that you will fail your final year. In this system that estimate has been converted into a fail flag, so you are obliged to take remedial courses; it is a cautionary signal, not a certainty. The three most influential factors in your assessment were your reason for choosing the school, your past class failures, and your intention to pursue higher education. Notably, all three pushed toward passing rather than failing: choosing the school mainly for home reasons is shared by about a quarter of students who passed; having no past failures matches the passing profile; and wanting higher education is true of every passing student in the comparison. The strongest ranked evidence therefore protects you. The failure flag appears to come from the overall combination of factors, including six absences versus an average of about four among passers and very high weekend alcohol use, which is rare among passing students. To improve, use the remedial support to build a steadier study routine, reduce absences, and review weekend drinking. Keep your higher-education goal and your clean failure record working for you, and ask for school or family support if your home internet or study time is limited.
